title: JIC Chief Inspects Ta Kwai Temple, Reports Cambodian Tank and Troop Buildup
detail: ACM Prapas Sornchaidee inspected Ta Kwai Temple and Hill 350 in Surin's Phanom Dong Rak district, reporting roughly 10 Cambodian tanks positioned 3-4km behind forward positions and troop assembly points about 2km from the Thai line, alongside intermittent Cambodian drone activity near the temple. He cited four Cambodian battalions (~500 personnel each) previously pushed back by Thai forces and alleged fortified bunkers financed by Chinese and Cambodian business interests. Officials said mines remain beyond the Thai perimeter, with three military dogs triggering a mine roughly a week earlier. Prapas said: 'We can be strong without provoking,' stressing Thailand's commitment to sovereignty within international law.

media.caption: JIC chief inspects Ta Kwai Temple and Hill 350 amid reported Cambodian tank buildup

title: Thailand Rebuts UN Rapporteur's Call to Allow Returns to Ban Nong Chan
detail: ACM Prapas Sornchaidee responded to UN Special Rapporteur Tom Andrews' call for Cambodian civilians to be allowed to return to the disputed Ban Nong Chan border area, saying any return must meet safety conditions under Clause 4 of the December 27 ceasefire statement, which permits returns 'in safety and dignity' to areas 'within their own side,' while Clause 3 assigns demarcation questions to the Joint Boundary Commission. Prapas noted Thailand and Cambodia agreed in October 2025 to a joint survey between boundary pillars 42-47, and said: 'Thailand is not rejecting humanitarian principles, but we must act responsibly. Safety must come first.'

media.caption: Thailand responds to UN rapporteur's call for civilian returns to Ban Nong Chan
